messages:
incbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT triggered — multiple customer reports: degraded connectivity from Redwood Private (VPC -> Azure South India) to on-prem via vWAN/ExpressRoute. Severity: P1-ish. Pager duty: on-call rohit_oncall.
rohit_oncall: Acknowledged. Paging network oncall and SRE. Taking initial lead.
pagerduty_bot: Alert -> rohit_oncall, devon_sre. Incident channel created.
devon_sre: on it — collecting scope. Which customers impacted? Maria, can you pull recent support tickets?
maria_ops: Pulling now, seeing 3 active customer alerts with RTP errors + timeouts since ~02:15 UTC. All on southindia region.
sanjay_net: I'm seeing BGP session flaps between our vWAN hub and Azure Edge routers in southindia. ASN 65535 -> remote ASN 12076; prefixes suddenly withdrawn then re-advertised.
devon_sre: Any correlation with DNS? Some customers report name resolution delays.
sanjay_net: Yes, query path crosses the same vWAN region. If BGP withdraws the preferred path, traffic reroutes through eastasia, causing high latency and some DNAT failures.
elaine_support: Customer-impacted apps: private inference endpoints (dedicated) — timeouts and 502s for config-heavy calls. Customers complaining about tail latency.
devon_sre: Mitigation plan: 1) stabilize BGP with Azure support 2) enforce route preference to avoid long detours 3) failover to Dedicated fallback region for critical customers.
rohit_oncall: Steps I'll run now: ssh into edge-router logs, check BGP neighbor status, capture syslog around 02:10-02:30 UTC.
sanjay_net: Commands:```show bgp neighbors 12076 all
show route-table vnet-hub
show ip bgp flap-statistics
``` Logs show repeated TCP session resets from remote peer.
devon_sre: Can we temporarily set community/local-preference to prefer direct ExpressRoute patch rather than the flapping egress?
sanjay_net: Yes. I'll push a policy to mark remote prefixes with local-pref 200 on our side. Doing it carefully to avoid AS-path changes.
maria_ops: Noted. Informing affected customers: sending ETA ~30-45m. (Draft message):
"We are investigating intermittent connectivity between Redwood Private and on-prem sites connected via Azure South India vWAN. Root cause appears to be BGP instability within the region; we are working with Azure and applying temporary route controls to reduce customer impact. Will update in 30 minutes"
elaine_support: Send now to the customers that opened tickets; include temporary workaround to retry requests and failover to our Dedicated endpoint in eu-west as a stop-gap.
rohit_oncall: Pushed local-pref policy at 02:36 UTC. Observing reduction in route withdrawals. BGP sessions stable for last 300s.
sanjay_net: Confirming — no withdrawals in recent 5 mins. Traffic shift looks healthy, latency back within SLO for most flows.
devon_sre: Good. Still seeing DNS cache misses for a handful of customers — likely due to earlier path swaps. Recommend flushing caches via our CDN edge config where possible.
maria_ops: Azure case opened #AZ-88912. Azure support says root cause: upstream peering flap at an ISP edge inside region; they pushed mitigations and monitored.
rohit_oncall: Customer impact summary for now: - 3 customers intermittently timed out on private endpoints between 02:15-02:40 UTC. - Primary mitigation: route preference change + Azure edge fixes. - No data loss reported.
devon_sre: Handoff time in 50 minutes to apac night oncall. I'll prepare a short runbook for the night shift: what to watch (BGP withdrawals, spikes in 5xxs, DNS NXDOMAINs), commands to run, how to rollback local-pref.
sanjay_net: Rollback command snippet in case of regressions:```no route-map PREFER_EXPRESS
clear ip bgp 12076 soft
``` Use caution — do not clear global BGP if customers are active.
maria_ops: Posted status update to status.redwood.ai and added affected regions list.
elaine_support: Notifying account execs for the impacted customers with interim mitigation details.
rohit_oncall: Adding timeline to channel: 02:14 UTC — first anomalies; 02:21 — pager alerts triggered; 02:36 — local-pref applied; 02:42 — Azure mitigation observed; 03:05 — system stable.
devon_sre: I'll keep monitoring for another 30m and then hand off. Postmortem owners: devon_sre (lead), sanjay_net (network root cause), maria_ops (customer comms).
incbot: INCIDENT status -> mitigated. Transitioning to monitoring. Please update when postmortem initiated. :white_check_mark:
rohit_oncall: Acknowledged. Leaving notes in PD ticket and closing the immediate alert playbook.
maria_ops: Will schedule postmortem meeting and collect logs + BGP dumps.
devon_sre: Thanks team. Good job reacting quickly. Final note: consider adding automated local-pref fallback for southindia if similar flaps exceed threshold (RFC: >3 withdrawals in 15m).
rohit_oncall: Handoff to night oncall @devon_sre in 30m. I'm standing down but will remain on-call if pager escalates. :thumbsup:
